name: GPS Broadcast Path & Ledger Depth Flywheel
description: Drives operator activation and retention by establishing the GPS broadcast path as the core value delivery mechanism. Zero-auth driver PWA enables immediate GPS ping emission on account creation, triggering ledger genesis events on Hyperledger Fabric. V/T ratio instrumentation surfaces fleet coverage health in PostHog, while Hour-4 and Hour-24 SMS nudges (Upstash Redis delayed jobs) recover accounts that have not yet emitted a first ping. As ledger history accumulates, the compliance-framed free-tier gate (30-day cap with loss-aversion prompt) converts operators to paid plans via M-Pesa STK push. The flywheel compounds: more GPS pings → deeper ledger history → stronger compliance narrative → higher upgrade conversion → more vehicles onboarded → more GPS pings.

functions.name: enqueuePing
functions.logic: Accepts a GpsPingPayload object containing latitude, longitude, accuracy, timestamp, device_token, vehicle_id, and cell_tower_fallback flag. Opens the 'ping_queue' IndexedDB object store and adds the payload as a new record with an auto-incremented key. If IndexedDB is unavailable, logs a warning and attempts an immediate POST to /api/gps/ping as a fallback. Returns a resolved Promise on success or rejects with an error on IndexedDB write failure.

functions.name: flushPingQueue
functions.signature: flushPingQueue(): Promise<{ flushed: number; failed: number }>
functions.logic: Opens the 'ping_queue' IndexedDB object store and reads all records in insertion order. For each record, POSTs the GpsPingPayload to /api/gps/ping with the device_token in the Authorization header. On a 2xx response, deletes the record from IndexedDB. On failure, leaves the record intact and increments the failed counter. Returns an object with flushed (number of successfully sent pings) and failed (number of pings that could not be delivered). Should be called whenever the online event fires on the window.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Parses the JSON body to extract latitude, longitude, accuracy, timestamp, device_token, vehicle_id, and cell_tower_fallback. Validates device_token against the devices table in PostgreSQL; returns 401 if invalid. Inserts a row into trip_events with all ping fields plus org_id resolved from the device record. If this is the first ping for the org (no prior trip_events rows for org_id), calls cancelNudgeJobs(org_id) and emits a PostHog 'first_gps_ping_received' event. Enqueues a Hyperledger Fabric write job by calling writeTripEvent with the ping payload. Returns 200 with { success: true, trip_event_id } on success, or 500 with an error message on failure.

functions.name: writeTripEvent
functions.signature: writeTripEvent(ping: GpsPingPayload & { trip_event_id: string; org_id: string; route_corridor: string }): Promise<{ tx_id: string }>
functions.logic: Connects to the Hyperledger Fabric gateway using the configured MSP identity and channel. Constructs a ledger transaction payload with fields: trip_event_id, vehicle_id, org_id, route_corridor, latitude, longitude, accuracy, accuracy_flag (boolean: accuracy < 50m), timestamp, and cell_tower_fallback. Submits the transaction to the 'TripEventContract' chaincode via the submitTransaction method. On success, returns { tx_id } where tx_id is the Fabric transaction ID. On failure, throws an error with the Fabric error details so the caller can retry via the job queue. Does not swallow errors — the job queue handles retry logic.

functions.name: computeVTRatio
functions.signature: computeVTRatio(vehicle_id: string, date: string, org_id: string): Promise<{ vehicle_id: string; date: string; vt_ratio: number; trip_count: number; expected_windows: number }>
functions.logic: Executes a DuckDB query over the trip_events table to count distinct trip windows (grouped by hour) for the given vehicle_id and date. Queries the expected_trip_windows table for the vehicle's scheduled windows on that date. Computes vt_ratio as trip_count / expected_windows, clamped to a maximum of 1.0. If expected_windows is 0, returns vt_ratio of null and logs a warning. Emits a PostHog server-side event 'vehicle_vt_ratio_updated' with properties { vehicle_id, org_id, date, vt_ratio, trip_count, expected_windows }. If vt_ratio < 0.5, adds a flag property 'below_threshold: true' to the PostHog event for downstream alerting. Returns the computed result object.

functions.name: enqueueActivationNudges
functions.signature: enqueueActivationNudges(org_id: string, phone_number: string, signup_at: Date): Promise<{ hour4_job_id: string; hour24_job_id: string }>
functions.logic: Creates two delayed jobs in Upstash Redis Queue. The first job fires at signup_at + 4 hours and sends an SMS to phone_number with a message framing GPS activation as a compliance requirement, including the org's onboarding link. The second job fires at signup_at + 24 hours with a stronger compliance-framed SMS referencing potential audit exposure. Both job IDs are stored in a Redis hash keyed by 'nudge:org:{org_id}' with fields 'hour4_job_id' and 'hour24_job_id'. Returns both job IDs so the caller can store them for later cancellation. If enqueue fails, throws an error — the caller should handle retry.

functions.name: cancelNudgeJobs
functions.logic: Looks up the Redis hash at 'nudge:org:{org_id}' to retrieve hour4_job_id and hour24_job_id. For each job ID that exists and has not yet fired, calls the Upstash Queue cancel API to remove the job from the queue. Deletes the Redis hash after cancellation. Returns { cancelled } array of successfully cancelled job IDs. If a job has already fired (Upstash returns 404), skips it silently. Idempotent — safe to call multiple times for the same org_id.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Extracts operator_id and plan_id from the JSON body. Checks Upstash Redis for an existing key 'mpesa_upgrade:{operator_id}:{plan_id}' — if present, returns 409 with { message: 'Upgrade already in progress' } to enforce idempotency. Fetches the operator's current ledger_event_count and days_until_cap from the ledger_stats view. Constructs a Daraja STK push request pre-populated with the upgrade amount for the selected plan, the operator's phone number, and an account reference that includes ledger_event_count for context. Fires the Daraja API STK push. On success, sets the Redis idempotency key with a 10-minute TTL and returns 200 with { checkout_request_id }. On Daraja API failure, returns 502 with the error detail.

integrations.description: Hyperledger Fabric network: GPS pings are written as ledger transactions via the TripEventContract chaincode. Each ping produces an immutable ledger entry with vehicle_id, route_corridor, accuracy_flag, and timestamp.
integrations.verification: curl -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/gps/ping -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"device_token":"test","latitude":-1.286389,"longitude":37.321,"accuracy":15,"vehicle_id":"v1","timestamp":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"}' && echo 'Check Fabric explorer for tx_id in response'

integrations.description: Upstash Redis Queue: delayed SMS nudge jobs are enqueued at signup (T+4h, T+24h) and cancelled on first GPS ping. Idempotency keys for M-Pesa upgrade are also stored in Upstash Redis.
integrations.verification: node -e "const { Redis } = require('@upstash/redis'); const r = new Redis({ url: process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, token: process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN }); r.hgetall('nudge:org:test_org').then(console.log)"

telemetry.description: Fires on every GPS ping successfully persisted to trip_events. This is the single most critical activation signal: it confirms the full broadcast path (driver PWA → ingest endpoint → PostgreSQL → Fabric queue) is functioning. The first INSERT per org_id marks Time-to-First-GPS-Ping, the primary success metric for this loop.

success_criteria: Time to First GPS Ping < 48 hours for > 60% of new operator accounts, measured as time between org creation and first trip_events INSERT per org_id
V/T ratio > 0.75 across active fleet portfolio at Month 2, measured via vehicle_vt_ratio_updated PostHog events aggregated per org
Driver PWA load time < 4 seconds on Safaricom 3G (400kbps / 400ms RTT), verified via Lighthouse CI on each deploy

Zero GPS ping loss rate due to connectivity drop — IndexedDB queue flush must deliver 100% of queued pings on reconnect, verified by comparing enqueuePing call count vs trip_events INSERT count per device session
Hyperledger Fabric write success rate > 99.5% per GPS ping ingested, measured as Fabric tx_id present on > 99.5% of trip_events rows within 60 seconds of INSERT
Free-tier ledger gate upgrade conversion > 15% of operators who see the FreeTierLedgerGate prompt complete an M-Pesa STK push upgrade within 7 days
Hour-4 SMS nudge delivery rate > 95% for accounts with no GPS ping at T+4h
Hour-24 SMS nudge cancellation rate > 80% — meaning > 80% of nudge-eligible accounts emit their first ping before the Hour-24 job fires
